paragraphs: Here's what I want you to see, friend. Jesus stays silent while liars pile up against Him, and then He speaks the truth when it costs Him the most. The high priest asks if He is the Christ, the Son of God, and Jesus answers, "You have said it yourself," and says they will see the Son of Man "sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven" (Matthew 26:63-64). He knew where that answer was heading, and He said it anyway.

Now look at Peter, because this one's close to home. He followed at a distance, sat down with the guards, and when the questions came, he said "I do not know the man!" (Matthew 26:72, 74). Three times, and the last time with cursing and swearing. Friend, I know I can be brave in my head and a puddle in the courtyard. Peter didn't fall apart over one big moment. He slipped over a few small ones, and the distance grew each time.

But hold on to the end of it. The rooster crows, Peter remembers what Jesus said, and he goes outside and weeps bitterly (Matthew 26:75). Jesus told him what was coming before it happened, and Peter's tears show that he knew it was real. This story isn't over, so don't close the book on Peter yet. When you've stumbled, remember what Jesus said and let it break your heart honestly, because Jesus isn't surprised by you.
